text:
emily: hey all, day 1. VPN says connected but ssh to bastion 10.40.1.2 times out. can ping 10.40.1.2 but traceroute shows packets leaving via my router. browser to intranet loads external login page.

oscar: welcome! sounds like asymmetric routing or LAN overlap. what's `netstat -rn` or `ip route` show?

emily: macbook, paste:
```
default via 10.2.0.1 dev en0
10.0.0.0/8 via 10.2.0.1 dev en0  <-- ISP uses 10.x
10.40.0.0/16 via 172.25.6.1 dev utun0
```

emily: so my ISP handed me 10.2.0.0/16 and it's winning for 10.40/16 because it's 10.0.0.0/8 route.

oscar: yep ISP CGN/Carrier using RFC1918 10.0/8 overlaps. two options: (1) add more specific route for 10.40/16 via your utun gw `sudo route -n add -net 10.40.0.0/16 172.25.6.1` (should work), (2) if OS prefers the 10.0/8 route due to metric you'll need to delete the broader route or add a host route for the bastion IP(s).

emily: added `sudo route -n add -net 10.40.0.0/16 172.25.6.1` and ssh connects now. thanks!

oscar: for persistence we usually push a LaunchAgent or fleet policy. i'll file a ticket to track ISP-overlap cases and add to onboarding doc.

devops-bot: Created INFRA-9999: "onboarding: ISP-assigned 10.0.0.0/8 overlaps corporate 10.40/16 causing asymmetric routing" assigned to @oscar.

emily: also saw Okta popup earlier, okta-bot reminded me to finish SSO before connecting. logged into Okta then reconnected VPN and route applied.

okta-bot: Reminder: finish Okta enrollment in default browser prior to VPN to ensure policies (route pushes) apply.

oscar: pro tip: tether phone hotspot while onboarding if ISP hands RFC1918 space; hotspots usually use 172/192 subnets and avoid collisions. adding note to new-hires.

emily: thanks all, fixed and ready for pairing! :)
